posts.body: We're running more buyer and lease leads than we can handle right now. New construction in San Antonio and Austin mostly, plus out-of-state relocations. Warm leads but they need vetting and nurturing. Most aren't transaction ready. If this sounds like something you'd take on, send me a DM.

I watched a seller turn down three offers last month because she was convinced her house was worth more. The agent just nodded and waited. I asked her what the comparable sales actually showed. She hadn't pulled them. Hadn't had the conversation. Just assumed the seller knew better.

That agent is still waiting for the market to shift. Meanwhile, the agent who priced a similar house down the street got four offers in ten days. Same market. Different approach.

The agents who stay consistent aren't the ones betting on market conditions. They're the ones who sit down with sellers and buyers and actually talk through what things cost right now. Not what they wish things cost. What they actually cost. That honesty builds trust. Trust builds momentum. Momentum builds business.

If you want to talk about what we're building at Lifestyle Design Realty, send me a DM.

Had a listing go sideways this week. Inspection came back with foundation issues the seller didn't disclose. Deal almost died right there.

1. The agent panicked and wanted to renegotiate everything. I told her to stop. We called the inspector back, got clarity on what was actually structural versus cosmetic. Turns out it was fixable and cheaper than everyone thought. The buyer stayed. Deal survived.

2. Most agents never make that second call. They assume the worst and kill momentum. One conversation changed the entire outcome.

3. This happens because agents operate alone. No one to sanity check the panic. No one to say "wait, let's think this through before we blow it up."

When you've got support, deals don't fall apart over miscommunication. You solve them.

We closed out Q4 with some real momentum. Not because we got lucky. Because our team showed up and did the work.

1. Consistency beats cycles. Markets shift. Leads go cold. But the agents here who keep their process tight and follow through actually close more when things get weird. They're not scrambling. They're executing.

2. Culture compounds. When you're around people grinding at the same level, you don't drop your standards. You raise them. That's what's happening here. Agents are pushing each other forward without me having to say a word.

3. Winning is contagious. One agent closes a tough deal, another agent sees it and believes their own deals are possible. Someone figures out a new way to work a lead, everyone learns from it. We're all getting better together.

Being part of a team that actually wins changes what you believe about yourself. That's what we're building.

When I started, I thought harder work solved everything. Long hours, more calls, grinding it out. That got me some deals. But it didn't get me ahead.

1. You can't scale solo. I spent five years trying. The ceiling isn't your work ethic. It's your time. Once I built a team and learned to delegate, everything changed.

2. Commission splits mean nothing if you have no support. I've seen agents take cuts at brokerages with real infrastructure and blow past what they made solo. The percentage looks smaller but the total gets bigger because you're actually supported.

3. Culture beats compensation every time. Agents will leave a higher split for a leader who actually invests in their growth. Money keeps people for a month. Real support keeps them for years.

If you want to talk about what we're building at Lifestyle Design Realty, send me a DM.

We have more buyer and lease leads than we can actually work right now.

Mostly new construction in San Antonio and Austin, plus out-of-state relocations coming in. The leads are warm but they need real vetting and nurturing before they're transaction ready. Most of these buyers aren't buying tomorrow. They're buying in three months or six months. If you're the kind of agent who knows how to work a lead that isn't hot yet and turn it into a closed deal down the road, we have inventory for you. If this sounds like something you'd take on, send me a DM.

Agents leave because their broker isn't actually there. You close a deal and nobody knows. You hit a problem and you're solving it alone at midnight. You want to grow and there's no plan, no support, no one pushing you forward. Here's what they're really looking for instead. 1. A leader who shows up. Not just quarterly. Not just when something breaks. Someone who knows what you're working on and genuinely cares if you win or lose. 2. Systems that actually work. Most brokers have nothing. You're inventing your process from scratch every deal. Better brokerages give you a playbook so you're not reinventing the wheel every month. 3. A culture where your split doesn't matter more than your growth. You can negotiate a commission all day. What you can't negotiate is whether your broker believes you're capable of bigger things. The right brokerage isn't about percentage points?
